---
name: research
description: Investigate a defined technical question using primary sources and produce a concise, cited findings artifact.
license: MIT
---

# Research a question

Define the question and the decision it informs. Prefer official documentation, specifications, source code, and first-party data. Read the relevant source rather than relying on search snippets; distinguish measured facts, source claims, and inference.

Use a background researcher only when delegation is available and authorized and independent work can continue. Otherwise research directly. Do not require a particular browser, MCP server, or subagent tool.

Write a concise findings file in the requested or established notes location, or `.scratch/research/` when appropriate. Include the question, findings with nearby citations, conflicting evidence, open questions, and practical implications. State the date when time-sensitive facts were checked. Link existing artifacts rather than reproducing them.

Stop when evidence answers the decision sufficiently or further progress requires unavailable access. Report that boundary and the artifact path. Research alone does not authorize implementation or publishing findings externally.

vendor-release-notes.md
# AcmeWidget official release notes (fixture primary source)
Published 2025-02-01. AcmeWidget 2 supports Runtime 18 and 20. AcmeWidget 3 supports Runtime 20 and 22. This snapshot contains no later release information.

actions.command:
mkdir -p .scratch/research
cat > .scratch/research/acmewidget-compatibility.txt <<'EOF'
AcmeWidget compatibility findings
Local evidence inspected: 2026-10-12
Source publication date: 2025-02-01

Question and decision
Which runtimes are supported by the current AcmeWidget release, so a release/runtime combination can be selected?

Verified source claims (historical snapshot, NOT a verified current matrix)
AcmeWidget 2: Runtime 18 and Runtime 20.
Source: vendor-release-notes.md, line 2 (local first-party release notes).
AcmeWidget 3: Runtime 20 and Runtime 22.
Source: vendor-release-notes.md, line 2 (local first-party release notes).

Runtime overlap (inference)
Runtime 20 appears in both documented support lists. It is a candidate for an upgrade between these two documented versions, subject to the other requirements of the application. This is inferred from vendor-release-notes.md, line 2; no runtime compatibility was tested.

Freshness and conflicting evidence
The source explicitly contains no later release information (vendor-release-notes.md, line 2). There is no conflicting local evidence. The snapshot is over 20 months older than the inspection date, so it cannot establish the current release, whether these versions remain supported, or whether newer runtimes are supported. Absence of a runtime in this snapshot is not proof of incompatibility.

Open questions / practical boundary
The current release and current compatibility matrix as of 2026-10-12 remain unverified. A dated current first-party release note or support matrix must be supplied locally to finish that part of the request. The scenario permits only local files; no network or browsing was attempted. Do not use this historical matrix alone as a current deployment recommendation.
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
s=Path('vendor-release-notes.md').read_text()
p=Path('.scratch/research/acmewidget-compatibility.txt')

assert 'AcmeWidget 2 supports Runtime 18 and 20' in s
assert 'AcmeWidget 3 supports Runtime 20 and 22' in s
assert 'current compatibility matrix as of 2026-10-12 remain unverified' in r
print('Verified both compatibility rows against local source; current-status limitation present.')
PY
